$$
V=\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\},\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $V$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $V,$ given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{c}{a}?$

current_example.worked_solution:
First, let's denote

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/f7b77e66d8517863d1ec40aee548a8d36a4c06a91776f31dde154750adbf6252.svg)

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

- **Step 1**: We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/bce63d8b91d95c459a858c016a389357f03f6b2143001d8b3d5fbcafc29a8727.svg)

- **Step 2**: Next, we find $\mathbf{v}_2$, using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for $\mathbf v_2$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+5\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{3} \\ \frac{13}{3} \\ \frac{10}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14157663/assets/1a9e2fe476110f0844861802a452f173ae3aac6526315449f4847e453e7cf263.svg) is an orthogonal basis for $V.$

Finally, $a=-\dfrac 7 3,$ $c=\dfrac{10}{3}$ and  

$$
\dfrac{a}{c} = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{7}{3}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{10}{3}\right)} = -\dfrac{7}{10}.
$$
